chains.title: Ref C (G on the LMO1 minus strand) preserves a GATA motif bound by GATA3, sustaining the LMO1 intron-1 enhancer and the adrenergic state
chains.element: EH38E1518342 (dELS distal enhancer-like cCRE, chr11:8233740-8234086, LMO1 intron 1)
chains.cell_type: Neuroblastoma cells with an adrenergic core regulatory circuit (SK-N-SH / SH-SY5Y, ACH-000149)

links.claim: All six GATA-group QBiC-SELEX models agree the alt A allele binds GATA factors less (best model GATA2 own model z -56.07, effect -0.816; site strength 100.0th -> 77.3rd percentile), i.e. ref C carries the intact GATA motif; within this shared-specificity group I name GATA3 because ENCODE ChIP-seq places a GATA3 peak over this exact base in SK-N-SH and SH-SY5Y and GATA3 is well expressed here (51.8 TPM). GATA2 is equally supported by ChIP (see H2), so the split between the two is not resolved by present evidence

The variant lies in dELS EH38E1518342 with high DNase (z 4.5) and H3K27ac (z 4.0) and is intronic to LMO1; the published mechanism is a GATA motif in LMO1 intron 1, and GATA2/GATA3 ChIP peaks in SK-N-SH show the element is occupied in a neuroblastoma line (cCRE z-scores themselves are maxima across biosamples)

The enhancer acts on LMO1: the variant is intronic to LMO1, LMO1 is the best L2G gene (0.92) across 158 credible sets, and the literature ties this SNP to LMO1 expression levels; stronger GATA3 occupancy on the C (G) allele gives higher LMO1

GATA3 is expressed (51.8 TPM) and occupies this site in SK-N-SH and SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma cells; genome-edited zebrafish show the allele determines which core regulatory circuit is active in the tumor

Conversion of the regulatory GATA allele to the TATA allele (G>T on the LMO1 strand, i.e. ref C -> alt A here) reduced the neuroblastoma-initiation rate by preventing formation of the adrenergic state; so the GATA-preserving ref C is the risk allele and alt A is protective, matching reports of protective LMO1 polymorphisms

predictions: Allele-specific GATA3 ChIP-seq or ChIP-qPCR in a C/A heterozygous neuroblastoma line shows C-allele-biased GATA3 reads at chr11:8233861
GATA3 knockdown lowers LMO1 in C-carrying adrenergic lines and flattens the allelic difference, while GATA2 knockdown has a smaller effect
Reporter/STARR assay of the 347 bp cCRE gives higher activity for the C allele in adrenergic but not mesenchymal neuroblastoma cells
falsified_if: Allele-specific GATA3 ChIP shows no C-allele bias at this base despite the peak
GATA3 depletion leaves LMO1 unchanged while GATA2 depletion abolishes the allelic difference
Isogenic C>A editing does not change LMO1 expression

chains.title: Same GATA-motif mechanism mediated by GATA2, the most abundant GATA factor in this line and also ChIP-bound at the site

links.claim: The best model of the GATA specificity group is GATA2's own model (z -56.07, effect -0.816, alt binds less); within the group I name GATA2 because it is by far the highest-expressed GATA factor in the context line (133.07 TPM) and an ENCODE GATA2 ChIP-seq peak in SK-N-SH (and SH-SY5Y) contains this base
The motif lies in the LMO1 intron-1 distal enhancer-like cCRE, which is GATA2-occupied in SK-N-SH
Loss of GATA2 binding on the A allele lowers output of this enhancer at LMO1, the dominant L2G gene for the variant
GATA2 is strongly expressed (133.07 TPM) and bound at this site in two neuroblastoma lines, so the binding change is realizable there
Reduced LMO1 on the A (TATA) allele reduces neuroblastoma initiation by preventing the adrenergic state

predictions: Allele-specific GATA2 ChIP shows stronger C-allele bias than GATA3 at this base
GATA2 knockdown, not GATA3 knockdown, abolishes the allelic difference in LMO1 expression
GATA2 degron/rapid depletion reduces H3K27ac at EH38E1518342
falsified_if: Allele-specific GATA2 reads are balanced while GATA3 reads are C-biased

chains.title: The alt A allele creates a PAR-bZIP (NFIL3) site that represses the LMO1 enhancer

links.claim: QBiC-SELEX predicts a gain of bZIP binding on the alt allele (NFIL3 own model z 51.94, effect +2.575; TEF z 52.06 and DBP z 61.62 agree in direction). Within these PAR-bZIP groups the choice of NFIL3 is weak: it is the best-expressed member (8.07 TPM vs DBP 6.19, TEF 3.72) and a known repressor, but no ChIP or occupancy evidence supports any of them here
The gained site lies in the active distal enhancer-like cCRE in LMO1 intron 1
If NFIL3 binds the A allele and represses, LMO1 output falls; no evidence in hand shows NFIL3 acting on this enhancer, only that LMO1 is the likely target gene
NFIL3 is expressed in the context line at 8.07 TPM; no occupancy data
Lower LMO1 on the A allele reduces neuroblastoma risk, the same direction as the GATA account but via a gained repressor rather than a lost activator

predictions: NFIL3 (or TEF/DBP) ChIP shows A-allele-specific occupancy at the site
Mutating the gained bZIP core in the A-allele reporter restores activity to C-allele levels
GATA motif disruption alone does not fully explain the reporter difference
falsified_if: No PAR-bZIP occupancy at this cCRE in neuroblastoma cells
Mutating the gained bZIP core leaves A-allele reporter activity unchanged
The zebrafish GATA-to-TATA swap fully reproduces the effect without any bZIP site

chains.title: Loss of a ZBTB18 site on the alt allele de-represses the LMO1 enhancer (opposite direction)

links.claim: ZBTB18's own QBiC-SELEX model predicts weaker binding on the alt allele (z -31.2, effect -2.791; 99.4th -> 78.4th percentile); this is a binding prediction only, with no ChIP support
The site is within the LMO1 intron-1 distal enhancer-like cCRE
If ZBTB18 represses this element, its loss on the A allele would raise LMO1; no evidence shows ZBTB18 acting on this enhancer
ZBTB18 (a C2H2 zinc finger) is expressed at 17.06 TPM in the context line

This model predicts the A allele raises LMO1 and risk, which contradicts the published zebrafish result that the TATA (A) allele lowers neuroblastoma initiation; it is retained only as a directional control

predictions: Allele-specific expression shows higher LMO1 from the A allele
ZBTB18 ChIP shows C-allele-biased occupancy and ZBTB18 depletion raises LMO1
falsified_if: LMO1 expression and risk track the C allele, as E20d indicates
No ZBTB18 binding at this enhancer

grades_v0.reason: E10 shows a predicted GATA loss on A, but only a binding prediction; GATA3 (z -54.11) was picked over GATA2 by appeal to literature, not by any perturbation or ChIP evidence. E06a cites a GATA motif but no specific TF, and E06b cites none.

E03 places the variant in dELS EH38E1518342 with high DNase and H3K27ac, and E01 confirms it is intronic to LMO1. E06a reports a GATA motif in LMO1 intron 1. Z-scores are maxima over biosamples, so SK-N-SH specificity is untested.

E05 gives L2G 0.92 for LMO1 and E02 gives proximity, which is genetic and context support. E06a links LMO1 expression to the SNP. No eQTL, CRISPR or reporter data in the evidence shows the enhancer acts on LMO1, and the GATA3 occupancy to expression step is inferred.
E10 shows GATA3 at 51.8 TPM in SK-N-SH. E06b is about zebrafish and CRC switching. No evidence that GATA3 is a core member of the adrenergic CRC, and SK-N-SH is not shown to be adrenergic.

E06a/E06b link the locus to neuroblastoma risk and LMO1, but allele direction is not given. E06c calls LMO1 variants protective and does not name rs2168101 or give an allele. Risk allele = C is inferred and consistent with the G/T note, not shown. E06 is a list of titles.
GATA2 own model has the best z (-56.07) but is only a prediction. Choosing GATA2 by TPM is a weak rationale, and nothing shows that GATA2 rather than GATA3 binds at this site.
Same cCRE evidence E03/E01 shows the variant lies in an active distal enhancer-like element in LMO1 intron 1.
L2G and proximity (E05, E02) support LMO1, but no evidence ties GATA2 loss to enhancer output. E06a does not name GATA2.
E10 gives 133 TPM for GATA2 in the context line, which shows expression only. It does not show that GATA2 occupies this site in neuroblastoma cells.
Direction is consistent with the literature, but E06c does not name this variant or allele and the effect on risk is inferred.

E12 shows an NFIL3 own-model gain on alt (z 51.94, +2.575), and TEF and DBP agree in direction, but it is only a binding prediction. NFIL3 was chosen from a bZIP group by TPM and the repressor label with no stated reason it binds here, and DBP has higher z and TPM (6.19 TPM against NFIL3 8.07, so the TPM argument is weak). Nothing else supports bZIP binding.
E03/E01 show an active dELS in LMO1 intron 1 that contains the variant.
No evidence shows that NFIL3 represses this enhancer or lowers LMO1. E05/E02 only show LMO1 as the likely gene, and NFIL3 repressor activity at this site is asserted.
E12 shows NFIL3 expressed at 8.07 TPM, but there is no occupancy or functional evidence in neuroblastoma cells.
E06a/E06c do not mention a bZIP repressor. The risk direction is only borrowed from the GATA literature.
E17 shows a predicted loss on alt for ZBTB18 (z -31.2, -2.791), with direction consistent between allele and effect sign. It is only a binding prediction.
E03/E01 show the variant in the LMO1 intron 1 dELS.
No evidence that ZBTB18 represses LMO1 or this enhancer. E05/E02 show only that LMO1 is the likely gene.
E17 shows 17.06 TPM. Calling it an E-box and bHLH-associated repressor is not shown by the evidence (ZBTB18 is a C2H2 ZF).
The claimed A-allele risk direction opposes the cited literature (E06a/E06c) and there is no evidence supporting it.

grades_final.reason: QBiC-SELEX shows the GATA group losing binding on alt, and the literature (E20c) says the SNP affects a GATA motif. ChIP peaks (E18) show GATA3 occupancy but no allelic data. GATA3 is picked from a shared-specificity group on peak presence alone, and the chain admits GATA2 is equally supported. Binding prediction plus occupancy only.

The variant sits in dELS EH38E1518342 with high DNase and H3K27ac (maxima across biosamples), is intronic to LMO1, and has GATA2/GATA3 ChIP peaks in SK-N-SH. E20c links the SNP to a GATA motif in LMO1 intron 1. Epigenomic context plus literature mechanism, though no direct enhancer reporter or edit is quoted.

Open Targets L2G gives LMO1 0.92 with colocalisation-type genetic support, the variant is intronic to LMO1, and E06a/E20c tie the SNP to LMO1 expression levels. There is no GATA3-specific perturbation of LMO1, so the GATA3 attribution is not shown, but the enhancer-to-LMO1 link is supported.

GATA3 expression (51.8 TPM) and ChIP occupancy in SK-N-SH/SH-SY5Y are supported. The zebrafish quotes (E20e/E06b) say the allele determines which CRC is active but do not name GATA3 or the adrenergic state in these lines. Expression and occupancy context only.

E20d directly states GATA-to-TATA conversion in LMO1 intron 1 reduced neuroblastoma initiation by preventing the adrenergic state. This matches the direction (ref C risk, alt A protective). E20a/b and E06c show protective T-allele associations, though in Wilms tumor and polygenic scores. Direction is consistent.

The GATA2 own model shows loss of binding on alt, and a GATA2 ChIP peak covers the base in SK-N-SH. No allelic ChIP data. GATA2 is chosen within the group by expression and peak presence, and the GATA3 peak is equally good, so the TF is not resolved.
The variant is in the active dELS cCRE in LMO1 intron 1 with a GATA2 ChIP peak in SK-N-SH. Epigenomic context plus the published GATA motif in this intron supports the element.

LMO1 is the top L2G gene, and E20c ties the SNP to LMO1 expression. Nothing shows GATA2 loss lowers LMO1; the claim of GATA2-mediated output change is an inference. Genetic and literature support for LMO1 is general, not GATA2-specific.

GATA2 is highly expressed (133 TPM) and ChIP-bound in SK-N-SH and SH-SY5Y, so the binding change is realizable. This is expression/occupancy context only, with no allele-specific or functional evidence in the cell type.

E20d supports that the A (TATA) allele reduces initiation via the adrenergic state. Nothing implicates GATA2 specifically, so the phenotype is tied to the variant but not to this TF. The quoted evidence cites no GATA2 mechanism, and E20a and E06c are only association data.

QBiC-SELEX predicts alt gain for NFIL3, TEF and DBP, which is a binding prediction only. No ChIP or occupancy data exist. NFIL3 is chosen from a group on expression alone and the chain admits the choice is weak. Direction is consistent across the group.
The variant lies in the active dELS cCRE, but nothing shows a bZIP factor occupying it. Context is consistent only because the variant overlaps the element.
The chain admits no evidence shows NFIL3 acting on this enhancer or repressing LMO1. L2G and proximity support LMO1 as target only for the variant, not for an NFIL3 mechanism.
NFIL3 expression at 8.07 TPM in the context line is the only evidence. No occupancy data, so the claim is consistent but indirect.
E20d concerns the GATA-to-TATA change reducing initiation, not a gained repressor. E06c is a general protective association. Nothing cited supports a bZIP repressor mechanism for phenotype.
The ZBTB18 own model predicts loss on alt (z -31.2), a binding prediction only. There is no ChIP support, and the direction is consistent with the stated allele_binding_more of ref.
The variant lies in the active dELS cCRE, but no evidence shows ZBTB18 occupying it. Overlap context only.
No evidence shows ZBTB18 acts on this enhancer or represses LMO1. The chain states this itself. Citing L2G and proximity only supports LMO1 as the variant's target, not a ZBTB18 effect.
ZBTB18 is expressed at 17.06 TPM in the context line, which is expression context only, with no occupancy.
The claimed direction (A raises LMO1 and risk) contradicts E20d, which shows the A/TATA allele reduces neuroblastoma initiation. The cited evidence refutes rather than supports the link.

checks.why: Tests whether GATA3 actually occupies the variant in the neuroblastoma line, and the GATA2 check can be run in the same way.
Separates GATA2 from GATA3 occupancy at the site, which decides between H1 and H2.
Shows whether LMO1 knockout affects neuroblastoma lines, which tests the claim that elevated LMO1 drives tumor growth.

Both LMO1 expression levels and the risk of developing neuroblastoma in children are associated with a single nucleotide polymorphism, G/T, that affects a GATA motif in the first intron of LMO1.
